decisions.decision: The bow-ADMG nonparametric latent-variable SCM is encoded as a `BowWitness`: a joint probability law on `Bool x Y x Y` for `(A, Y 0, Y 1)` together with an observed-outcome coordinate, with the assumption `POConsistency` imposing `Y = Y(A)` almost surely.
decisions.why: For the bow ADMG `A -> Y`, `A <-> Y` with an unrestricted latent `U` parenting both, the achievable joint laws of `(A, Y(0), Y(1))` are exactly ALL joint laws on `Bool x Y^2` (take `U` to be the triple, `A = f_A(U)`, `Y = f_Y(A,U)`). The encoding is therefore complete and faithful, and it is literally the construction the note's own proofs use (`U = (A, Y(0), Y(1))`, `Y = Y(A)`). Encoding the same class through `Causalean.SCM.Model.SCM` / `Causalean.PO.Core.POSystem` would add a dependent SWIG-node / regime layer that the note never exercises, at a large proof cost and no gain in faithfulness.

decisions.decision: `D_f(P || Q)` is defined locally as an EXTENDED-VALUED, integrability-total divergence: `noncomputable def fDiv (f : Real -> Real) (P Q : Measure Y) : EReal := if Integrable (fun x => f ((P.rnDeriv Q x).toReal)) Q then ((integral (fun x => f ((P.rnDeriv Q x).toReal)) Q : Real) : EReal) else (TOP : EReal)`, over Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.Measure.rnDeriv`. Every divergence constraint in the plan is the EReal inequality `fDiv f P Q <= ((divRadius f e : Real) : EReal)`, so membership in any ball ENTAILS integrability rather than silently defaulting on it. Three small build-inline companion lemmas make the convention faithful and are listed in `Helpers/Divergence.lean`: (i) `fDiv_measurable` -- `x |-> f ((P.rnDeriv Q x).toReal)` is measurable, from continuity of an `AdmissibleGenerator` on `Set.Ici 0` and measurability of `rnDeriv`; (ii) `integrable_negPart_of_ac` -- for an `AdmissibleGenerator f` and probability laws with `P << Q`, convexity gives a subgradient `b` at 1 with `f t >= b * (t - 1)`, and `r = dP/dQ` is Q-integrable with `integral r Q = 1`, so the NEGATIVE part of `f r` is dominated by `|b| * (r + 1)` and is always Q-integrable; hence the honest extended Lebesgue integral of `f r` is well defined in `[0, TOP]` and equals `TOP` exactly in the `else` branch, i.e. `fDiv` never lands in `BOT` and the `if`-convention is not a silent default but the true value; (iii) `fDiv_lt_top_iff` / `integrable_of_fDiv_le_real` -- `fDiv f P Q <= (B : EReal)` for a real `B` gives back the `Integrable` hypothesis. Consequently the Jensen reuse `MeasureTheory.le_integral_rnDeriv_of_ac` (whose signature, verified by `lean_loogle`, is `ConvexOn R (Set.Ici 0) f -> ContinuousWithinAt f (Set.Ici 0) 0 -> Integrable (fun x => f ((mu.rnDeriv nu x).toReal)) nu -> mu.AbsolutelyContinuous nu -> f (mu.real univ) <= integral ...`) is invoked ONLY where its `Integrable` premise is discharged from a hypothesis actually in hand -- either from ball membership via (iii), or, in the chord/upper-bound direction, from `dP/dQ <= c` making `f o r` bounded (f continuous on the compact `[0, c]`) hence integrable on a probability space. It is NOT claimed to follow from the `AdmissibleGenerator` assumptions alone.
decisions.why: Neither Mathlib nor Causalean carries a general f-divergence: re-checked at round 3 with `lean_leansearch 'f-divergence of measures defined as integral of convex function of Radon-Nikodym derivative, extended real valued'` -> only `InformationTheory.klDiv` / `klFun` / `toReal_klDiv_eq_integral_klFun`, plus `Measure.rnDeriv` and `setIntegral_rnDeriv_smul'`; `lean_local_search 'fDiv'` -> only this project's own local declaration; Causalean has only `Stat.chiSqDiv` and `Stat.tvDist` (no EReal anywhere in the tree). The generic convex-generator layer therefore has to be introduced here. Round-2 review correctly flagged the previous real Bochner-integral encoding: `MeasureTheory.integral` returns 0 on a nonintegrable integrand, so a generator whose divergence is genuinely `+infinity` would have been silently recorded as `0 <= B_f(e)` and admitted into every ball -- an unsound over-large class, and a reuse of `le_integral_rnDeriv_of_ac` whose `Integrable` premise no arbitrary finite continuous convex generator supplies. The EReal `if Integrable then . else TOP` encoding is the same convention Mathlib itself uses for `klDiv` (`klDiv_def`, `klDiv_eq_integral_klFun`); `EReal` rather than `ENNReal` because an admissible `f` may be negative on `[0,1)` (e.g. `f_KL t = t log t`), so nonnegativity of the divergence is a THEOREM (extended Jensen, via (ii)) rather than something pre-baked into the value type.

Consistent with F1-D7 (the frozen `source.{cite, locator, carrier}` travels as sibling scalars, `carrier: logical-claim` in both cases) and with the exclusion of both nodes from `local_id`s and the manifest (F1-D6).

env.world: A fixed covariate stratum of a binary-treatment potential-outcome system on a standard Borel outcome space \(\mathcal Y\). A nonparametric latent-variable structural causal model has observed vertices \(A\in\{0,1\}\) and \(Y\in\mathcal Y\) carrying the bow ADMG \(A\to Y\), \(A\leftrightarrow Y\); it is realized by the joint law of \((A,Y(0),Y(1))\) on \(\{0,1\}\times\mathcal Y^2\) with latent \(U=(A,Y(0),Y(1))\) and \(Y=Y(A)\). The arm index is \(a\), the arm propensity is \(e=\Pr(A=a)\in(0,1)\), and the observed arm law is \(P=\mathcal L(Y\mid A=a)\). Candidate interventional laws \(Q=\mathcal L(Y(a))\) and residual laws \(R=\mathcal L(Y(a)\mid A\ne a)\) range over \(\mathcal P(\mathcal Y)\); the compatible classes \(\mathfrak M_e(P)\), \(\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)\) and the mixture classes \(\mathfrak L_e(P)\), \(\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\) are subsets of \(\mathcal P(\mathcal Y)\). When \(\mathcal Y=\mathbb R\) the threshold \(y\), the distribution functions \(F_P,F_Q\), the event probability \(p=F_P(y)\), the binary coordinates \(q,q_0,\varepsilon\), the endpoint maps \(L_e,U_e,L^{\to}_e,U^{\to}_e\), the bounded query \(h\in L^\infty(P)\) and its endpoints \(\underline\theta_h,\overline\theta_h\) live in this same stratum.

env.world: The \(f\)-divergence geometry over \(\mathcal P(\mathcal Y)\) attached to a fixed propensity \(e\in(0,1)\) with likelihood-ratio cap \(c=1/e\). Generators \(f\) range over the finite continuous convex functions \(f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\) with \(f(1)=0\); the divergence is \(D_f(P\|Q)=\int_{\mathcal Y}f(dP/dQ)\,dQ\), taken as an extended-real quantity in \([0,+\infty]\), and the calibrated radius is \(B_f(e)=ef(1/e)+(1-e)f(0)\). The extended reading is forced and harmless: when \(P\ll Q\) the likelihood ratio \(r=dP/dQ\) satisfies \(\int r\,dQ=1\), and convexity gives a subgradient \(b\) at \(1\) with \(f(t)\ge b(t-1)\), so the negative part of \(f(r)\) is dominated by \(|b|(r+1)\) and is always \(Q\)-integrable; the integral is therefore always well defined, is nonnegative by Jensen, and equals \(+\infty\) exactly when \(f(r)\) fails to be \(Q\)-integrable. A divergence constraint \(D_f(P\|Q)\le B_f(e)\) is thus in particular an integrability requirement on the pair \((P,Q)\), and an arbitrary admissible generator supplies no integrability by itself. Distinguished generators are the Kullback--Leibler generator \(f_{\mathrm{KL}}(t)=t\log t\), the propensity hinge \(f_c(t)=(t-c)_+\), and the propensity-adaptive family \(f_e(t)=(t-1/e)_+\); the exactness frontier is the affine-equivalence class \(\mathfrak H_c\). The induced ambiguity classes are \(\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\), \(\mathfrak B^{\to}_{f,e}(P)\) and their legality-corrected intersections \(\mathfrak B^{\mathrm{law}}_{f,e}(P)\), \(\mathfrak B^{\mathrm{law},\to}_{f,e}(P)\); \(\mathcal O_f\subset(0,1)^2\) is an open region of binary pairs, coordinatized on a finite alphabet by the cellwise weights \(p_j,q_j\), and \(e_1,e_2\in(0,1)\) are two distinct propensities.

The data are one fixed measurable sequence \((A_i,Y_i)_{i\ge1}\) of maps from the underlying probability space to \(\{0,1\}\times\mathcal Y\); independence and the identical observed law are properties asserted of that same sequence, and every estimator, band and coverage statement below is computed from it. With \(n_a=\sum_i\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}\), the observable estimators are the empirical propensity \(\widehat e_n=n^{-1}\sum_i\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}\) and the arm-conditional empirical distribution function \(\widehat F_{P,n}(y)=n_a^{-1}\sum_{i:A_i=a}\mathbf 1\{Y_i\le y\}\) when \(n_a>0\). The inference objects are the threshold-indexed set-valued band \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}:\mathbb R\to\mathcal P([0,1]^2)\) and the directional-inference handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{dir}}\).

env.world: One global covariate-augmented nonparametric latent-variable structural causal model on standard Borel spaces \(\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\), with observed vertices \(X,A,Y\), observed arrows \(X\to A\), \(X\to Y\), \(A\to Y\), and a latent variable \(U\) that may be a parent of each of \(X,A,Y\). The covariate law is \(\mu_X\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X)\); the propensity system \(\boldsymbol e=(e_0,e_1)\) consists of measurable maps \(\mathcal X\to[0,1]\) with \(e_0(x)+e_1(x)=1\) and \(e_a(x)\in[\kappa,1-\kappa]\) for a uniform overlap constant \(\kappa\in(0,1/2]\). Canonical declaration for this node is the `structure`: alongside the `positivity` member field it carries the mutual-absolute-continuity clause `MutuallyAC Q P` and the extended-valued divergence bound `fDiv f P Q <= (divRadius f e : EReal)` as non-member fields, and `jkBallSet` is the derived companion `def` (F1-D9).

INTEGRABILITY IS PART OF MEMBERSHIP (round-3 fix): because `fDiv` takes the value `TOP` exactly when `f (dP/dQ)` is not Q-integrable, and `divRadius f e` is a real number, the bound `fDiv f P Q <= (divRadius f e : EReal)` is FALSE for a nonintegrable pair instead of silently reading off the Bochner default `0`. Build-inline.

thm:conditional-adaptive-hinge-exactness.notes: Paper-owned; the combined field-tier frontier. Build-inline. Search trace: as for S2 + S4. Key REUSE: `Measure.rnDeriv_le_one_iff_le` turns the vanishing hinge integral into the measure cap `e_a P_a <= Q_a` fiberwise; `Measure.MeasureDense.approx` carries the measurable-carrier set S_C of equation (4) from the countable algebra to all Borel sets. Remaining build-inline work: 'a nonnegative integrand with zero integral vanishes a.e.' (Mathlib `MeasureTheory.integral_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg`) and the joint Borel measurability of `(a, x, t) |-> (t - 1/e_a x)_+`. Under the EReal `fDiv` of F1-D4 this theorem needs no extra hypothesis: the hinge integrand `(r_x - c_ax)_+` is nonnegative and dominated by `r_x`, which is `Q_a(x, .)`-integrable by `Measure.integrable_toReal_rnDeriv`, so each fiberwise `fDiv` is real (never `TOP`), the constraint `fDiv <= (0 : EReal)` is equivalent to the note's `integral (r_x - c_ax)_+ dQ_x <= 0`, and the vanishing-a.e. step then gives the cap. No Jensen/`le_integral_rnDeriv_of_ac` premise is required anywhere in this proof.

file_plan.contents: Thin barrel importing every shared helper subsystem.

Shared substantive predicates used to state universal exactness, open binary illegality, query endpoints, total-variation locality, and conditional likelihood-ratio cap classes without duplicating them across theorem files.

The nine assumption Props (BowStructure, POConsistency, StrictPositivity, MutualAbsCont, IidObservationalSampling, CondBowArchitecture, CondOverlap, CondConsistency, CondReverseSupport) plus the two witness carriers `BowWitness Y` and `CondBowWitness X Y`; IidObservationalSampling is the finite first-`n` predicate required by F1-D10 and does not claim a whole-sequence IIDSample bridge.
def:bow-compatible, def:bow-compatible-one-sided, def:mixture-class, def:mixture-class-one-sided (structures + set forms).

The EReal integrability-total `fDiv` (F1-D4), divRadius, AdmissibleGenerator, def:jk-ball, def:jk-ball-one-sided, def:hinge-class, def:lawful-correction, def:lawful-correction-one-sided, plus the affine-invariance and chord L-lemmas and the four integrability L-lemmas the extended encoding requires: `fDiv_measurable`, `integrable_negPart_of_ac` (subgradient domination `f t >= b (t - 1)` plus `Measure.integrable_toReal_rnDeriv`, giving `fDiv <> BOT` and making the `TOP` branch the honest `+infinity`), `integrable_of_fDiv_le_real` (a real bound excludes `TOP` and returns the `Integrable` premise of `le_integral_rnDeriv_of_ac`), and `integrable_of_rnDeriv_le` (a bounded likelihood ratio `dP/dQ <= c` makes `f o (dP/dQ)` bounded, hence integrable, which is what licenses integrating the chord bound on the mixture class).
L-lemmas: mixture identity <-> measure inequality e*P <= Q <-> likelihood-ratio cap dP/dQ <= 1/e; the residual-law construction R = (Q - eP)/(1-e); the R << P <-> Q << P equivalence.

L-lemmas: full-support binary laws from `bernoulliLaw`, the two-cell divergence formula `fDiv_bernoulli` (including the `Integrable`-is-automatic step that makes the EReal `fDiv` real and equal to `q f(p/q) + (1-q) f((1-p)/(1-q))` on a two-cell alphabet), its continuity on (0,1)^2, and the two-ratio (lambda, y, x) witness constructor.
def:cdf-maps, def:cdf-maps-one-sided and their algebra (range, monotonicity in e and p, boundary values).
The six conditional class definitions (bow-compatible one-sided / mutual, mixture one-sided / mutual, adaptive-hinge ball one-sided / mutual).

L-lemmas: the measurable residual-kernel construction via `Measure.measurable_of_measurable_coe`; the countable-algebra -> all-Borel extension of a fiberwise measure inequality via `Measure.MeasureDense.approx`; uniting armwise/cellwise exceptional sets into one conull set; the product-kernel SCM assembly.

The two frozen cited-gate propositions HoeffdingBoundedMean and DkwMassartCdfBand, each a named `Sort 0` declaration with no proof, threaded as explicit hypotheses into TFiniteSampleSimultaneousBand.lean (F1-D5).

def:honest-band, def:directional-handle (+ directionalHandleRecipe and IsRectangularBand), the arm-conditional empirical propensity and cdf -- all indexed by the same sample sequence `Z` that `IidObservationalSampling` constrains (F1-D10) -- and the rectangular-hull propagation L-lemmas. The tie theorem carries `hBandMeas` directly; no separate measurability predicate is declared here.

substrate_survey.reason: The SCM/do-calculus stack is a SWIG-node, regime-indexed graphical-identification layer; this note never runs a graphical algorithm and works entirely with the joint law of (A, Y(0), Y(1)) (resp. (X, A, Y(0), Y(1))), for which the bow ADMG with unrestricted latent U imposes no restriction at all (F1-D1).
No d-separation, c-component or Markov-equivalence question arises: the single graph in the note is the fixed two-vertex bow, used only to license an unrestricted latent common parent.

Surveyed via API.md; the partial-ID content lives under Causalean/PO/ID/Partial/ and is scalar-interval / LP / support-function shaped. The interval vocabulary IS reused (see below); the LP and response-function machinery is not applicable to a set of laws on a standard Borel space.

`IdentifiedInterval`, `identifiedInterval_eq_Icc`, `identifiedInterval_param_Icc` are the exact vocabulary for the two sharp CDF-endpoint theorems (sharp interval as the range of an objective over a feasible set, with the convex-mixture path giving order-connectedness for free).

The MSM / Dorn-Guo calibrated stack and the chi-square l2Ball are Omega-level reweighting ambiguity sets built on condExp and Hilbert-space support functions; this note's classes are subsets of `Measure Y`. Recorded on def:lawful-correction and thm:query-legality-correction as the technique reference for 'intersect an over-wide ambiguity set with the data-compatibility constraint and show strict tightening'.
`POSystem` / `Consistency` are dependent regime-indexed structures over `Regime V X`; the note's consistency is the one-line selector identity `Y = Y(A)` on a concrete product space.

`bernoulliBool_bind` is literally the mixture identity Q = eP + (1-e)R produced by the latent draw; `bernoulliLaw` supplies every full-support binary witness in the two dichotomy theorems and both generator-frontier necessity proofs.

`IIDSample` is the analogous whole-sequence sampling bundle, but the frozen assumption is deliberately first-`n` and therefore does not definitionally bridge to it. The same raw sequence `Z` is retained and shared with `honestBand` and both consumers; `cdfStat` remains reusable, while the random-denominator arm-conditional empirical CDF is build-inline. `hoeffding_abs_ge` is the near-fit recorded against the cited Hoeffding gate.

Found at round 5 while re-searching the flagged cited-gate closure. This module does the whole arm-conditioning step of thm:finite-sample-simultaneous-band: `MarkedIID` is the finite marked-iid bundle matching this note's `IidObservationalSampling`, `MarkedIID.selectedOutcomes_conditionalLaw` proves the retained arm-`a` outcomes are conditionally iid with the arm law given the complete mark word, `measure_le_of_cond_le_on_finite_partition` averages over the word partition, and `conditionalMarkedSubsample_dkwRadius` / `conditionalMarkedSubsample_empiricalCDF_tail` turn a SUPPLIED fixed-size empirical-CDF tail bound into the random-arm-count guarantee at exactly this note's radius `dkwRadius alpha m = sqrt (log (4/alpha) / (2*m))`. It deliberately does NOT prove DKW--Massart -- the fixed-size bound is its hypothesis -- so it is a reuse for the conditioning/lifting and leaves lem:dkw-massart-cdf-band a genuine cited gate.

Single-generator divergences only; the note quantifies over all admissible convex generators, so a general `fDiv` is introduced locally (F1-D4), EReal-valued with the `if Integrable then . else TOP` convention that Mathlib itself uses for `klDiv` -- `Causalean` carries no `EReal` code at all (grep confirms), so nothing here is displaced. `tvDist` and its tensorization are recorded on thm:tie-inclusive-band-impossibility as the technique reference for the n-fold product total-variation bound.

`measure_eq_bind_marginal_condDistrib` is the disintegration chain rule for integrating the product kernel against mu_X; `GraphMapProd.mechanismKernel` / `map_graph_prod_eq_compProd` are the 'exogenous noise + structural mechanism = composition product' pattern that the conditional completeness proof's equation (3) instantiates.

`Measure.MeasureDense.of_generateFrom_isSetAlgebra_finite` + `Measure.MeasureDense.approx` are exactly the countable-algebra-to-all-Borel approximation the two conditional theorems need; without this the plan would have had to rebuild a monotone-class argument.

`rnDeriv_le_one_iff_le` is the cap-vs-measure-inequality bridge used by every completeness theorem; `Measure.integrable_toReal_rnDeriv` gives Q-integrability of the likelihood ratio, which underwrites both the negative-part domination that makes the EReal `fDiv` honest and the hinge-class integrability; `le_integral_rnDeriv_of_ac` is the Jensen half of the divergence lower bound, usable ONLY where its explicit `Integrable` premise (verified by lean_loogle at round 3) is already discharged -- from ball membership or from a bounded likelihood ratio -- never from the generator assumptions alone.
